players.product: data-center electrical contracting (The Superior Group), data-center fiber/interconnection buildout and power-delivery infrastructure

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Jose Mas: Q2 revenue was $4.374 billion, up 23% year over year; adjusted EBITDA was $384 million, up 40%; adjusted EPS was $2.22, up 49% - all above guidance, with EBITDA margins up 100 basis points versus last year's second quarter and new highs across virtually every key financial metric.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue $4.374 billion (+23%); adjusted EBITDA $384 million (+40%); adjusted EPS $2.22 (+49%); EBITDA margin +100 bps

quarterly_data.signal: Backlog reached a record $21.4 billion at quarter end, a nearly $5 billion year-over-year increase and a $1 billion sequential organic increase (roughly 5% sequential, 30% year over year), with total-company book-to-bill over 1.2x. CEO: nearly $2.5 billion of backlog growth over the past two quarters contributes only modestly to 2026 revenue, with the majority expected to benefit 2027; the Q2 growth came from normal-size projects, not from the large pursuits, and MasTec expects backlog to end 2026 higher than today, led by power delivery, clean energy and infrastructure, and pipeline.
quarterly_data.figure: backlog $21.4 billion (nearly $5 billion YoY increase, $1 billion sequential organic); book-to-bill over 1.2x; nearly $2.5 billion backlog growth over two quarters

quarterly_data.signal: Raised full-year 2026 guidance including Superior: revenue of $18.2 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $1.6 billion and adjusted EPS of $9.30 (year-over-year growth of 27%, 39% and 42%); Q3 guidance revenue $4.9 billion, adjusted EBITDA $482 million, adjusted EPS $2.98; over $1 billion of 2026 cash flow from operations, the majority in Q4. CEO: the revision removes $400 million of communications revenue and adds about $800 million of Superior revenue with $100 million of EBITDA; legacy EBITDA unchanged at $1.5 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue $18.2 billion (+27%), adjusted EBITDA $1.6 billion (+39%), adjusted EPS $9.30 (+42%); Q3 revenue $4.9 billion, EBITDA $482 million, EPS $2.98

quarterly_data.signal: MasTec closed the acquisition of The Superior Group in July (the largest in its history): Superior expands electrical infrastructure capabilities within mission-critical facilities and data centers with approximately 3,000 team members, operates largely standalone and is reported in Power Delivery. CEO Jose Mas: Superior's $1.4 billion backlog (as of May) was similar to how MasTec would look at its backlog build, with an update due next quarter; customer conversations on cross-selling have gone 'unbelievably well', Superior is in addition to the organic 2028 targets set at the May Investor Day, and its enhanced margins drive a second-half margin that is hundreds of basis points higher than the first half.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 3,000 team members; Superior backlog $1.4 billion (May)

quarterly_data.signal: Mission-critical / data centers (CEO Jose Mas): demand is unprecedented with 'no end in sight'; the recent turnkey data center project (awarded in Q4 last year) is progressing well with multiple sister companies on it, MasTec is in the midst of several large pursuits and 'fully expect[s] additional awards in 2026'. MasTec's mission-critical exposure as a percentage of revenue has been smaller than peers' and is still in its early stages at scale; CEO sees reports of state data-center bans or pauses as 'a little bit overblown' and the states named as not strong MasTec geographies.

Power Delivery Q2: revenue approximately $1.25 billion (up nearly 20%), EBITDA $113 million (up 24%), margins just over 9% (up over 30 basis points year over year, up 220 basis points sequentially); record backlog of approximately $6.3 billion (up nearly $1.3 billion year over year) with 1.1x book-to-bill, and an excellent start to Q3 bookings. Demand is driven by utility spending on transmission, hardening and reliability, grid expansion and data center power needs. Outlook: Q3 including Superior about $1.6 billion of revenue with low double-digit EBITDA margins; full-year about $5.725 billion with low double-digit margins (CEO: embedded legacy Power Delivery margin 9.8%).
quarterly_data.figure: revenue ~$1.25 billion, EBITDA $113 million (+24%); backlog ~$6.3 billion; Q3 ~$1.6 billion; FY ~$5.725 billion; legacy margin 9.8%

quarterly_data.signal: Clean Energy and Infrastructure Q2: revenue over $1.6 billion (up 43%), EBITDA $128 million (up 54%); backlog approximately $7.8 billion, up roughly $500 million sequentially (book-to-bill 1.3x), driven by renewables. Outlook: Q3 revenue approximately $1.9 billion (40% growth) with high single-digit margins; full-year approximately $6.8 billion. CEO: the number of power-generation pursuits (simple-cycle and RICE engines) has increased materially; renewables are 'I would say' 60%-65% solar at this point, with wind resilient and good backlog into 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue over $1.6 billion (+43%), EBITDA $128 million (+54%); backlog ~$7.8 billion; Q3 ~$1.9 billion; FY ~$6.8 billion; 60%-65% solar

quarterly_data.signal: Pipeline Infrastructure Q2: revenue approximately $643 million (up 19%), EBITDA approximately $119 million (18.4% margin, nearly doubled); backlog approximately $1.8 billion, up 35% sequentially (book-to-bill 1.7x), the highest since Q2 2023, including a newly signed project for 2027 work. Q3 outlook about $645 million with mid-teens margins; full-year largely unchanged. CEO: power-generation demand is driving customer commitments to future gas deliveries; 'We feel really good about 2027. We feel amazing about 2028 and 2029', with the back half of 2027 expected to be a lot bigger than the first half.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue ~$643 million (+19%), EBITDA ~$119 million (18.4%); backlog ~$1.8 billion (+35% QoQ); Q3 ~$645 million

quarterly_data.signal: Communications Q2: revenue approximately $890 million and EBITDA $73 million (about 8.2% margin), with execution challenges and higher fuel and equipment costs. Full-year communications revenue cut to approximately $3.25 billion (high single-digit margins, about 100 basis points lower year over year); Q3 about $800 million. CEO: wireless is waiting for new spectrum whose equipment will not be available until next year, and wireline is hit by RDOF projects rolling off and delayed starts on wins at a couple of wireline customers; the reduction is roughly 50/50, maybe a little more skewed to wireless; second-half margins are expected about 200 basis points above the first half. MasTec continues to win hyperscaler connectivity work and is pursuing billions of dollars of such opportunities, including multiple projects north of $1 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue ~$890 million, EBITDA $73 million (8.2%); FY ~$3.25 billion; Q3 ~$800 million

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Jose Mas: since the May Investor Day visibility has significantly improved and the number of large pursuits has significantly increased; outside communications MasTec is more bullish in all segments than two and a half months ago. On the FCC inverter ban, CEO: no impact on its projects for at least the next few years. CFO Paul DiMarco: unapproved change orders are just over $200 million, ordinary-course timing.
quarterly_data.figure: unapproved change orders just over $200 million
